A +13.6pp gap on the Qatar side. Bosnia and Herzegovina v Qatar in FIFA World Cup 2026 is the match. The model has Qatar stronger than the market does — that's the reason this fires as a Pick rather than a Pass.

On Elo, Bosnia and Herzegovina comes in 20 points ahead — Bosnia and Herzegovina at 1660, Qatar at 1640. Both Elo numbers are pulled live from the public Elo source. No host, home-ground, or altitude adjustments apply here; the prior reads straight from Elo.

Three-way split from the model: Bosnia and Herzegovina to win at 38%, the draw at 29%, and Qatar to win at 34%. Draw share decays with Elo gap; on a fixture this evenly matched the draw carries more probability than a casual reader might guess. Qatar on the win side reads 34%.

On the same three-way, Polymarket: Bosnia and Herzegovina to win at 56%, the draw at 25%, and Qatar to win at 20%. Polymarket has Qatar at 20%, which prices out at American odds of +400; the model has the same side at 34%. The +13.6pp gap across them is the disagreement we're surfacing.

Bootstrap discipline matters most on the longshots — wide bands on small point estimates collapse the Pick rate fast. On Qatar the lower bound is 29%, which keeps the lower-bound gap at +8.7pp against the market — past +3pp, so the Pick clears. The engine isn't arguing reputation, recency, or narrative. It's reading the underlying numbers and finding Qatar priced shorter on the market than the prior supports — that's the disagreement.

What would close this gap: confirmed team news that pulls the prior down on the side we like, a venue or weather change, or a tournament suspension landing before kickoff. With kickoff 33 days out, the refresh is weekly until we cross five days, then daily, then hourly inside the final day. A Pick this wide doesn't collapse on small news; a narrow one can flip to Pass on a single refresh. Either way, the engine republishes and the page reflects the latest read.
